topic: the watching-eyes effect — a photo of eyes made people pay 3x more for honesty-box coffee
title: A Photo Of Eyes Made People Pay 3x More For Coffee
description: A university coffee stand tripled its honesty-box payments just by taping up a photo of eyes — no camera, no rule change, just a stare. AI-narrated commentary on the psychology behind why watching eyes, even fake ones, change how we behave. #psychology #shorts

hook_candidates.text: Taping a photo of eyes to a wall tripled what people paid for coffee.
Why would a printed photo of eyes make people pay three times more for their coffee?
You'd think only a real camera keeps people honest — a flat photo of eyes did almost the same job.
For ten weeks, a university coffee room quietly swapped a flowers banner for a pair of eyes, then just counted the cash.

beats.text: Taping a photo of eyes to a wall **tripled** what people paid for coffee.
Ten weeks, one office coffee stand, eyes swapped in for flowers — and **payments** jumped every time.
Your brain can't tell painted eyes from real ones watching — two dots make you **honest**. What changes when eyes are on you?
